overallNotes: Kelli Ann Brotherton (42yo, born 1982-11-14) is a revenue-cycle lead at Gem Valley Rural Health Network outside Emmett, Idaho. She is married to Travis (feed store assistant manager), has a stepdaughter Mikayla (21, dental assisting student), and cares for her father Gary Sipes (71, on dialysis). Her 3-year arc (2025–2028) moves from overwhelmed operational fixer to recognized system-builder: she built a network-wide denial-reduction system, survived a catastrophic software go-live that reversed gains, developed hypertension requiring medication, and eventually produced three straight quarters of sustained improvement. Home pressures include aging pickup repairs, a pet euthanasia (Juno, blue heeler), strained finances, and a gradually steadier marriage built on explicit communication. Kelli is an ISTJ who prefers plain language, measurable targets, and practical tools over theory. Her identity arc is from 'the person who gets handed the ugly pile' to someone who can say 'I built and enforced the operating discipline' without apology. She discovers preferences for slow, low-agenda travel (Oregon coast), dry workplace comedies over heavy dramas, rural healthcare memoirs over crime novels, and 1990s country music with some early-2000s pop-country added. Core relationships: Monica Wren (CFO, leadership ally), Shawna Haskell (friend/coding classmate, work vent), Dr. Owen Leland (family medicine physician, operational stakeholder). Data quality issues: all 30 slices have truncated 'focus' fields (quote-based auto-generation that cuts at ~70 chars), 12 slices have truncated summaries, and all emotional_tone values default to 'neutral' rather than reflecting actual sentiment. Tags are too broad (work/family/health as generic buckets) and lack specificity for searchability.
